news.hook: Josh Jacobs stood in court and told the judge he fully understands the seriousness and takes full responsibility for the altercation at his home.
news.name: Packers' Josh Jacobs Pleads No Contest to Misdemeanor Charges
news.summary: On Thursday, Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges from a May 23 incident at his Wisconsin home. He agreed to a $1,000 fine, restitution, counseling, and a 12-month deferred judgment on the property charge, avoiding jail time as long as he stays out of trouble and has no contact with the victim. Packers coach Matt LaFleur stood by Jacobs' character despite the situation, while the NFL keeps him on the Commissioner’s Exempt List with no set timeline for potential discipline like a two-to-six game suspension.

news.summary: ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from the University of Texas campus ahead of the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, with both undefeated teams coming off blowout Week 1 wins—Ohio State 56-3 over Ball State and Texas 59-7 over Texas State. Fans fired up the rivalry with playful jabs like a sign mocking Ohio State coach Ryan Day for putting ketchup on brisket, a nod to Texas barbecue pride that even GameDay called out as 'No, just no.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian kept it simple: 'We're talking about a hell of a football game that's gonna get played tonight.' The Longhorns are slight 1.5-point home favorites, airing on ABC.

news.hook: Cam Coleman seemed to snag the deep ball over his shoulder, but it popped loose on impact—right into Jaylen McClain's waiting hands for a wild Ohio State pick.
news.name: Jaylen McClain's Fluky Interception Stuns Texas in Ohio State Clash
news.summary: In the first quarter of the top-ranked Buckeyes' primetime matchup against Texas in Austin, quarterback Arch Manning targeted wide-open receiver Cam Coleman on a deep route. Coleman hauled it in mid-air but lost control hitting the turf, allowing Ohio State safety Jaylen McClain to scoop the live ball at the Buckeyes' 19-yard line. The turnover followed Texas' earlier fumble and preserved Ohio State's 3-0 lead after a field goal, capping a rough start for the home team's offense amid a packed stadium.

news.hook: Players stepping onto the turf in Austin will face a brutal 163-degree heat reading under the primetime lights. It's the ultimate test for these undefeated title contenders.
news.name: No. 1 Ohio State Faces No. 4 Texas in Scorching Austin Showdown
news.summary: Both teams roll into DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium perfect after dominant Week 1 wins, rematching recent clashes where Ohio State held the edge. The game kicks off at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC, with Texas a slim 1.5-point favorite and the total at 49.5 points amid heavy betting action. Analysts favor the home Longhorns, fans split predictions online, and the extreme heat—confirmed by reporters—promises a grueling battle between top-ranked rivals.

news.hook: With the field turf hitting 163 degrees under the Austin sun, Texas' Cam Coleman had Arch Manning's deep pass right in his hands—only for it to bounce straight to an Ohio State defender.
news.name: Ohio State Jumps Ahead of Texas in Scorching 163-Degree Showdown
news.summary: No. 1 Ohio State grabbed an early lead over No. 4 Texas in Austin's Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, where pre-kickoff field temperatures reached 163.6 degrees amid 97-100 degree air. Texas QB Arch Manning's deep shot to wideout Cam Coleman deflected off for a wild interception, sparking debate over whether receiver drops should count as QB stats, as former NFL QB Robert Griffin III noted. Ohio State's opportunistic defense cashed in for a 10-3 edge by the second quarter, boosted by WR Jeremiah Smith's explosive plays.

news.hook: Patrick Mahomes fires off behind-the-back and no-look passes like it's nothing, headphones on, looking sharp in the indoor facility. Chiefs fans can't wait for his return.
news.name: Mahomes Drops Slick Training Video Before Chiefs Opener
news.summary: The quarterback shared an Instagram clip of his effortless throws ahead of the Chiefs' 2026 home opener against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football. Cleared from a torn ACL and LCL injury from December 2025, Mahomes appears fit and slim, drawing praise for his generational talent. Fans shared the video widely, posting clocks and declarations that the team is back, with Arrowhead Stadium buzzing just two days out.

news.hook: Kayden McDonald, the Texans' hyped second-round pick, sprained his ankle in practice and now faces at least four weeks out right before the season opener.
news.name: Texans Place Rookie DT McDonald on IR, Sign Crumedy
news.summary: Houston placed rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald on injured reserve after he sprained his ankle during Wednesday's practice, missing the next two sessions and the opener against the Buffalo Bills. The 6-foot-3, 326-pound Ohio State product, last year's Big Ten Defensive Lineman of the Year, can return as early as Week 5. To replace him, the team signed 6-foot-4 defensive tackle Jaden Crumedy, a former sixth-round pick who played for the Panthers and Packers' practice squad, adding needed depth to the defensive line.

news.hook: Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz watched Kansas's pregame video on 'Bleeding Kansas' history and felt embarrassed for them. That fire helped his Tigers dominate 38-21.
news.name: Missouri Coach Blasts Kansas Hype Video After 38-21 Border War Win
news.summary: Kansas's 'Heroes and Villains' video highlighted Civil War-era clashes like abolitionist John Brown and slavery conflicts, framing the rivalry as deeper than sports. Drinkwitz called it 'right-versus-wrong bullcrap,' motivated his team to pull away in the second half with QB Austin Simmons' three TD passes, Jamal Roberts' 125 rushing yards and a score, plus defensive turnovers. He quipped postgame, 'We left Kansas bleeding again,' and wondered aloud if the rivalry should continue if it gets 'weird' like that—especially with unity needed after 9/11. The win marked Missouri's fifth straight in the series, played at Kansas's David Booth Stadium.

news.hook: Coach Lane Kiffin stepped off the bus in sunglasses and a green jacket, flashing a peace sign next to a grinning Lil Wayne pointing out the window.
news.name: Lane Kiffin Walks with Lil Wayne and Boosie Before LSU Game
news.summary: LSU fans cheered as Kiffin led the Tiger Walk down Victory Hill with rap stars Lil Wayne and Boosie ahead of Saturday's game against Louisiana Tech. Lil Wayne rocked an LSU shirt, yellow pants, and a purple cap while joining former star Tyrann Mathieu, as the official account dubbed it 'LilWeezyana State University.' This follows last week's star guests like Livvy Dunne, building hype for the No. 8 Tigers after their 51-10 win over Clemson. Fans loved the Baton Rouge flavor, with posts calling it pure local aura.
